findings.title: src/d091/dedup-without-unique.ts — SELECT-then-INSERT dedup on `d091_contacts` with no unique constraint behind it
findings.taxonomy: SELECT-then-INSERT dedup with no unique constraint
findings.evidence: Heuristic "dedup-without-unique" matched a single-row read of `d091_contacts` on `tenant_id`, `external_ref` followed in the same function by an insert writing those same columns, while no UNIQUE or PRIMARY KEY constraint on `d091_contacts` covers them.
findings.impact: The read and the insert are two round trips with no lock between them, so two concurrent callers both see 'absent' and both insert. The duplicate is silent at write time and surfaces later as an error on every `.maybeSingle()` reading that predicate — a read-path outage produced by a write-path race, long after the deploy. SCOPE: constraints are read from the migration DDL and a root schema snapshot only, so one added by hand in a dashboard is not seen; the read and the insert must be in the same function, so a dedup split across a helper is not assessed; and a table this pass never saw declared is skipped rather than reported.
findings.fix: Add `unique (tenant_id, external_ref)` on `d091_contacts` in a migration and let the database arbitrate — then either upsert on that constraint (`.upsert(…, { onConflict: "tenant_id,external_ref" })`) or catch the duplicate-key error and re-read. Application-side dedup cannot be made correct without it.
cwe: CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')

findings.title: pages/api/cross-file-orders.js — authenticated route hands a client-supplied id to `listOrdersForTenant()`, which scopes its query by it
findings.taxonomy: Object-level authorization gap across a module boundary
findings.evidence: Heuristic "bola-cross-file": the handler authenticates the caller (binding `session`) and passes a request-rooted value to `listOrdersForTenant()`, imported from `lib/order-repo.ts`, whose parameter `tenantId` reaches `.eq("tenant_id", tenantId)` on a service-role `.from()` chain — with no comparison against `session` in either function.
findings.impact: The caller is authenticated but never authorized for the object: any signed-in user can name another tenant's or user's tenant_id and the repository will return those rows, because the service-role client bypasses RLS and this scoping is the only gate. SCOPE: one import hop only (route → repository, not route → service → repository); the callee must be an exported function or arrow const taking the value as a named parameter; and an ownership comparison performed in a THIRD module is not seen, so confirm no such check runs before treating this as unmitigated.
findings.fix: Pass the verified session identity into `listOrdersForTenant()` and scope on that, or compare the request's tenant_id against `session`'s and reject a mismatch — in the repository, so every caller inherits the check.
cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

findings.title: src/inngest/import-inbound.ts — service-role `select` on `gmail_inbound_messages` in a background-job path with no tenant predicate
findings.taxonomy: Service-role query in a background-job path with no tenant predicate
findings.evidence: Heuristic "job-tenant-scope": a service-role `.select()` on `.from("gmail_inbound_messages")` in a background-job path (src/inngest/import-inbound.ts) carries no tenant-scoping predicate (`.eq`/`.in`/`.filter`/`.match` on a tenant/owner column). Annotate a site `// d091-allow:service-role-tenant` if a wrapper or RPC enforces scoping the AST can't see.
findings.impact: A background job runs with no request or session, so the service-role client bypasses RLS and this query reads (or writes) rows across every tenant. With no explicit tenant filter, one tenant's job can expose or mutate another tenant's data — exactly the class of ATC finding #2003.
findings.fix: Scope the query to the job's tenant (e.g. `.eq("tenant_id", tenantId)` from the job payload/context) at every cited call site, or if a wrapper/RPC already enforces tenancy, annotate each site `// d091-allow:service-role-tenant`.
cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

findings.title: pages/api/isr-rebuild-secret.js — `REVALIDATE_SECRET` verified with no rotation-pair acceptance window
findings.taxonomy: Static secret verified with no rotation-pair acceptance window
findings.evidence: Heuristic "secret-rotation-pair": the secret `process.env.REVALIDATE_SECRET` is verified with a single === process.env.REVALIDATE_SECRET and no sibling rotation variant (e.g. `REVALIDATE_SECRET_PREVIOUS`) is read anywhere in the codebase, nor does the comparison accept more than one secret.
findings.impact: Rotating this secret is a hard cutover: the moment the new value is deployed, every in-flight request still signed with the old value is rejected. A dual-secret window (accept current AND previous during rollover) removes that outage.
findings.fix: Accept both the current and a previous secret during rotation — read a `REVALIDATE_SECRET_PREVIOUS` (or equivalent) alongside `REVALIDATE_SECRET` and pass the verify if EITHER matches, then retire the old value after the window.

findings.title: Log-only catch continues after a failure at a request boundary
findings.taxonomy: M1 — Swallowed exception at request boundary
findings.evidence: `catch (err)`: the catch only records the error and then falls through without recovery or a typed failure.
findings.impact: A failed security- or request-boundary operation can continue as though it succeeded, weakening denial and transaction guarantees.
findings.fix: Propagate or wrap the error, return an explicit typed failure, terminate the path, or perform a documented compensating action.
findings.okWhen: The catch has an explicit ignored-error rationale for genuinely best-effort work, or it rethrows, returns typed failure, compensates, or terminates.
findings.notOkWhen: The catch is empty, only logs and continues, or returns a value indistinguishable from success.
cwe: CWE-754: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions

findings.title: Unjustified `as any` bypasses TypeScript
findings.evidence: Escaped expression: `raw`; the assertion introduces `any`, disabling static checks for this expression, and no runtime validation/narrowing boundary is visible.
findings.impact: The compiler can no longer prove the value matches the promised type, moving failures to production and obscuring the actual boundary contract.
findings.fix: Validate or narrow at the boundary and keep the resulting type, or document the concrete interop constraint beside the narrowest possible assertion.
findings.okWhen: A runtime validator or narrowing guard proves the value, or a concrete interop rationale explains the smallest necessary assertion.

findings.impact: A recoverable library failure can terminate the hosting process or force callers to add an unsafe recovery boundary.
findings.fix: Return a descriptive error and let the application boundary decide whether the process must terminate.

findings.title: Python exception handler silently discards a failure

findings.impact: Callers can continue as though the operation succeeded while the original failure is hidden.
findings.fix: Propagate or wrap the exception, return an explicit failure, compensate, or document a narrowly justified ignored exception.

findings.title: Production-independent assertion: Python assert
findings.evidence: Python assert uses True. `True` is a fixed passing condition and does not read a production-derived value.
findings.impact: This assertion can keep passing after the production behavior it appears to cover changes or disappears.
findings.fix: Assert a production-derived return value, state change, emitted argument, or other observable behavior instead of a fixed condition.

findings.title: SECURITY DEFINER public.promote_to_admin exposes arbitrary-ID data
findings.evidence: Takes id parameter(s) target_user_id and uses them in the query with no caller (auth.uid()/auth.jwt()) constraint — returns data for arbitrary IDs.
findings.impact: Callable by anon, authenticated — any authenticated caller can pass an arbitrary id and read another tenant/user's row.
findings.fix: Add a caller-scoping predicate (auth.uid()/auth.jwt()) to the query, or REVOKE EXECUTE from anon/authenticated if the function isn't meant to be client-callable (check RLS policies don't depend on it first).
findings.notOkWhen: The function returns or mutates rows for the passed id without also checking that id belongs to the calling user/tenant.
findings.okWhen: The query additionally constrains by auth.uid()/auth.jwt(), or the id parameter is only ever the caller's own (enforced elsewhere and provably unspoofable).
